findings.population: adults with chronic neuropathic pain (postherpetic neuralgia and other conditions)
findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review found the high-concentration (8%) capsaicin patch produced more participants with meaningful pain relief than low-concentration creams, with a number needed to treat of about 8.8 in postherpetic neuralgia — an effect the reviewers judge similar to other chronic-pain therapies, typically used when others have failed.
findings.limitations: evidence is for the clinician-applied 8% patch, not over-the-counter low-concentration creams; NNT of ~9 means most treated patients do not achieve meaningful relief

findings.population: adults with acute, sub-acute, or chronic low back pain (Cochrane review, 10 trials, ~1,600 adults)
findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review found strong evidence from two high-quality trials that Harpagophytum procumbens standardized to 50 or 100 mg harpagoside daily beat placebo for short-term low back pain and rescue-medication use, with another high-quality trial showing rough equivalence to rofecoxib 12.5 mg/day.
findings.limitations: short-term evidence only; the review found no evidence on long-term safety or usefulness

findings.population: adults with low back pain (same Cochrane review)
findings.finding_summary: The same Cochrane review found moderate evidence from two trials that Salix alba standardized to 120 or 240 mg salicin daily beat placebo for short-term pain and rescue medication, with one trial showing rough equivalence to rofecoxib 12.5 mg/day.
findings.limitations: moderate (not strong) evidence grading; no long-term safety data; salicin is an aspirin-family compound with the corresponding cautions

findings.population: adults with arthritis, mostly osteoarthritis (29 RCTs, 2,396 participants)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis (29 RCTs, 2,396 participants; doses 120-1,500 mg for 4-36 weeks) found curcumin and Curcuma longa extract significantly decreased pain and improved physical function and stiffness, with efficacy similar to NSAIDs in the trials making that comparison, and no safety signals.
findings.limitations: the authors caution that trial quality is low and quantity per arthritis type small; overlaps with the existing curcumin rows — this row anchors the whole-extract (turmeric) evidence

findings.population: adults with migraine (n=55, 3-month randomized controlled trial)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized placebo-controlled trial, riboflavin 400 mg/day reduced migraine attack frequency (p=0.005) and headache days (p=0.012), with 59% of riboflavin patients improving at least 50% versus 15% on placebo (number needed to treat 2.3) and only minor adverse events.
findings.limitations: single 55-patient trial is the anchor; later systematic reviews judge the overall evidence base supportive but limited

findings.population: adults with migraine (10 oral-magnesium trials, 789 participants, within a 21-study meta-analysis)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis found oral magnesium significantly reduced migraine frequency and intensity (odds ratios 0.20 and 0.27 versus control), alongside intravenous magnesium's acute-attack effects.
findings.limitations: several included trials lacked adequate randomization methods; complements the modest blood-pressure row staged in batch 10
